jobs.occupation: Product Engineer - R&D - Construction
jobs.description:
Be the bridge between Norwegian municipalities and a team that builds with AI every day.

As part of the departmentWe are building software that powers the entire construction lifecycle from first sketch to final handover. Our solutions lead the Nordic market, and we're trusted by companies across the region to keep their projects running smoothly.

We are looking for a Product Engineer to join our team in Tønsberg with 5+ years of technical experience in software development and a good understanding of construction products, you can bring a customer and domain perspective to the way we build and test our software. The team is both developing and maintaining the ByggSøk application – a modern, cloud-based solution that simplifies and streamlines the entire building permit process for professionals in the construction industry, from planning to submission and communication with municipalities. We deliver about 50% of all digital building permit applications submitted to local authorities in Norway.

This is a product-focused role in a team that is increasingly built around AI. You will spend more of your time working with AI tools and agents than writing code by hand: turning domain knowledge and customer needs into well-defined solutions, directing AI to build, test and document them, and making sure what we deliver is correct, secure and actually useful for our users. You will be the person who knows ByggSøk and the Norwegian building permit domain inside out, and who speaks with our Norwegian customers, municipalities and stakeholders on the team's behalf.

The team is continuously improving collaboration, automation and integrations between professionals, municipalities and national services – helping shape the future of digital building permit solutions in Norway. The team runs on Scrum and uses Jira, Confluence, GitHub and Claude Code.

Your primary workplace will be in Tønsberg, where you'll collaborate with your immediate team, though we offer flexibility for remote work when appropriate. We place high value on collaboration, and you'll be working alongside talented professionals at all levels, both locally and globally.

Your role:

• 
Own the understanding of ByggSøk – its functionality, users, regulations and integrations – and act as the link between customers, municipalities, business and the development team.

• 
Shape the product: gather and clarify needs, write and refine requirements and user stories, and help prioritise the backlog.

• 
Use AI tools and agents (such as Claude Code and Copilot) to prototype, implement, test, analyse and document solutions, and review and quality-assure what they produce.

• 
Continuously find new ways to apply AI to make the team, the product and our customers' workflow more efficient.

• 
Participate in Norwegian-language meetings, workshops and customer dialogue, and communicate clearly with the international team in English.

• 
Work closely with developers and testers in Scrum, contributing to code and technical decisions where it makes sense.

What you bring:

• 
Fluent Norwegian, ideally native level, both written and spoken – this is a must, as you will lead and attend meetings and talk with Norwegian customers and authorities daily

• 
Good English communication skills, both written and verbal

• 
Available to work on site in Tønsberg

• 
Hands-on experience using AI tools in daily work, and a curiosity and drive to explore what they can do

• 
5+ years of technical experience in software development.

• 
Strong ability to learn and understand project details and domain knowledge – experience from the construction industry, public sector, building permits (byggesak) or similar regulated domains is a strong advantage

• 
Experience from product, solution, business analysis, consulting or software roles, working in an agile team

• 
Technical understanding of modern web solutions – a background as a developer or experience with .NET, Angular/TypeScript or SQL is an advantage, but deep coding skills are not required

• 
Familiarity with Jira, Confluence, GitHub is an advantage

• 
A structured, curious and responsible way of working, with the ability to communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical people

Why join EG?We hire ambitious and curious people who want to make an impact. Here, you’ll work with leading technology and real industry challenges, with the opportunity to learn and grow alongside talented colleagues. You’ll be trusted with real responsibility and the freedom to take ownership, while being part of a global community where we collaborate and grow across teams, functions and borders.We look forward to hearing from you! If you would like more information before you apply, please contact Szymon Graczyk, Team Manager on sgrac@eg.dk. We evaluate applications on an ongoing basis and hire when the right candidate is found. So please send your CV and application as soon as possible, using the apply button in the job ad. All inquiries are handled confidentially.

At EG, we build software that makes a difference.Our industry-specific software helps people and businesses work smarter every day, from doctors spending more time with patients to builders running safer and more efficient projects. Built by people who understand the industries we serve and backed by EG’s scale, our software keeps key processes running smoothly, so people can focus on what matters.

Join us in creating software that works for people, not software that makes people work.

Visit our career pages to meet some of your future colleagues, explore our culture, and watch our video "We Make a Difference".

Learn more about EG here.

jobs.occupation: Drone Builder / Drone Mechanic
jobs.description:
Aviant delivers food and medicine to people's gardens using drones. After starting in the labs at MIT in 2020, we have flown over 10,000 flights, covered tens of thousands of kilometers and currently operate the largest commercial base for last-mile drone delivery in Europe, at Ski just outside Oslo. Demand is growing faster than our fleet, and we now need to build a lot more drones. We are therefore looking for hands-on Drone Builders / Drone Mechanics to join our workshop and help us scale up production.

As a Drone Builder, you will:

• 
Build and assemble new drones, from components to flight-ready aircraft

• 
Wire, solder and crimp harnesses, connectors and power systems

• 
Install and test motors, servos, batteries, flight controllers and other electronics

• 
Do composite work, repairs and replacement of airframe parts

• 
Run bench tests and quality checks before handing drones over to flight operations

• 
Perform scheduled and unscheduled maintenance on our operational fleet

• 
Follow and improve build instructions, checklists and documentation, so every drone is built the same way, every time

• 
Find smarter ways to build faster with higher quality (jigs, fixtures, kits, 3D-printed parts)

Relevant technology:

• 
Aircraft type: Fixed-wing VTOL, 2.5m wingspan

• 
Methods: Soldering, crimping, 3D printing, CNC, metalworking

• 
Materials: Composites (CFRP, GFRP), wood, metal, plastic

• 
Components: BLDC motors, servos, lithium batteries, flight controllers, PCBs

• 
Tools: Multimeter, hand and power tools, technical drawings and CAD

Ideal candidate:

• 
Loves to work with your hands and takes pride in doing things properly

• 
Extremely structured and detail-oriented. In aviation, small mistakes matter

• 
Has practical experience from building or repairing things, such as drones, RC aircraft, cars, bikes, electronics or aircraft

• 
Is comfortable with soldering and basic electronics

• 
Hungry for results and motivated by seeing your work fly

It's a plus if you have:

• 
A trade certificate (fagbrev) or education as e.g. aircraft technician, electrician, automation technician or industrial mechanic

• 
Experience with composites, 3D printing or series production

• 
Experience from aviation maintenance or other quality-controlled production

No drone experience is required. You will be trained in Aviant's build and maintenance procedures.

What we offer:

• 
Work on introducing a new means of transportation into society. Like building the first cars, you can tell your grandkids that "I was part of making this happen"

• 
See the drones you build fly real deliveries to customers every week

• 
Work in the leading environment in Europe for these systems

• 
Large stock option package. When we succeed, we all succeed!

Practical:

• 
Position: 100%, on-site

• 
Start: As soon as possible

• 
Location: Ski, Norway (10 min train from Oslo)

• 
Language: Norwegian or English

• 
Process: A short first interview, followed by a practical hands-on test in our workshop

• 
We review applications continuously and hire as soon as we find the right people, so apply early!

If you want to build the drones that make drone delivery a reality, please apply!

jobs.occupation: PhD Candidate in Reliability Science for AI-Enabled Systems
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 8,6000 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
We are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate to join our research activities in reliability science for AI-enabled systems.

The PhD project will focus on developing methods to understand, assess, and improve the reliability and trustworthiness of AI-enabled systems. The research will address challenges arising when AI becomes an integral part of systems where failures or incorrect decisions may have significant operational, economic, environmental, or safety consequences.

The candidate will work in an interdisciplinary research environment combining reliability engineering, artificial intelligence, prognostics and health management, and industrial decision support. The position offers opportunities for collaboration with academic and industrial partners and for participation in international research activities.

Are you motivated to take a step towards a doctorate and open up exciting career opportunities? As a PhD Candidate with us, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education and research, in and outside academia.

You will be supervised by Professor Janet Lin.
Duties of the position
• Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate
• Carry out research of good quality within the framework described above
• Academic publications and popular science dissemination
• Participate in the RAMS research group (RAMS - MTP - NTNU)
• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions
• Collaborate with academic and industrial partners when relevant.
Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Required selection criteria
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty's Doctoral Programme, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information.
• You must have a relevant Master's degree in mechanical engineering, industrial engineering, computer science, or equivalent. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis
• Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position.
• You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works.
• You must have good written and oral English language and communication skills
• You must have a documented academic background in at least one area relevant, such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, reliability engineering, prognostics and health management, data analytics, automation and control, or related methods
The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria
• Knowledge of or experience with artificial intelligence and machine learning methods.
• Knowledge of reliability engineering, prognostics and health management (PHM), condition monitoring, maintenance, or safety-critical systems.
• Experience with programming, data analysis, modelling, or simulation using relevant tools and languages.
• Experience with research-oriented work, for example through a Master's thesis, scientific publications, research projects, or other relevant research activities.
• Experience with industrial applications or interdisciplinary research involving engineering and artificial intelligence is an advantage.
• Knowledge of or interest in topics related to trustworthy AI, such as uncertainty, robustness, explainability, verification and validation, or AI safety, is an advantagePersonal characteristics
To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: 

• Work independently and take responsibility for progressing your research
• Work in a structured way, set goals and make plans to achieve them
• Show curiosity, creativity, and strong motivation for the research area
• Analyze complex problems, assess different perspectives, and draw well-founded conclusions
• Communicate and collaborate effectively with researchers and other relevant partners
Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.
We offer
• An exciting job with an important mission in society
• Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment
• Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period
• Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues
• Working capital that can be used to implement the project
• Mentor programme as a new employee at NTNU
• Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK)
• Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2)
As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits.
Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.

At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality.
Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,- per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. 

The employment period is 3 years.

For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Engineering within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme through out the period of employment.

As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them.

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to bein conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed.
About the application
The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in English.

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

The application must include:

• Transcripts and diplomas for Bachelor's and Master's degrees
• CV 
• Copy of Master's thesis. If you have recently submitted your Master's thesis, you can attach a draft of the thesis. Documentation of a completed Master's degree must be presented before taking up the position.
• Project outline containing proposals for an overall description of research questions, theoretical perspectives, methodological design for the project and progress plan (maximum 1500 words/4 pages) 
• Short letter of motivation (400 words/1 page)
• Possibly publications etc. other relevant research work
• Possibly certificates
• Names and contact information of three relevant referees
If all, or parts, of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both Bachelor's and Master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution uses “diploma supplement” (normal for most European institutions), you must attach this. A description of the documentation required can also be found here. If you already have a statement from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), please attach this as well.

Joint work will be considered. If it is difficult to identify your contribution to joint work, you must attach a brief description of your participation.

When assessing the best qualified, we emphasize necessary qualifications such as education, experience and personal suitability. Motivation for the position, ambitions, and potential for research will also count when assessing the candidates.NTNU recognizes a wide range of academic contributions and has committed itself to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment and CoARA (responsible assessment of research and recognition of a greater breadth of academic contributions in accordance with NTNU's social mission).
General information
A public list of applicants with name, age, job title and municipality of residence is prepared after the application deadline. If you wish to be exempt from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the exemption is not granted.

If you think this position looks interesting and in line with your qualifications, you are welcome to apply.

If you have any questions about the position, please contact Professor Janet Lin, e-mail: janet.lin@ntnu.no. 

If you have any questions about the recruitment process, please contact HR Senior Consultant Hedda Winnberg, e-mail: hedda.winnberg@ntnu.no.

The position
Do you want to contribute to research about non-coding RNAs in sperm health and infertility?

A PhD position is available at the Department of Clinical Medicine, Faculty of Health Sciences in the Translational Vascular Research group, working on the project ´Developmental non-coding RNA signatures of sperm health and infertility´

The Translational Vascular Research group includes both basic scientists and clinicians. We perform research spanning across disciplines, from the analysis of patient samples to laboratory based investigation of cell behaviour. Parts of our research group are based at Karolinska Institute/KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm, Sweden, with the opportunity for close collaborations with these institutes.The fertility department at the Women’s clinic at the University Hospital of North Norway (UNN) is a collaboration partner and will contribute with expertise in andrology and analysis of semen samples.

The position is for a period of four years. The nominal length of the PhD program is three years. The fourth year is distributed as 25% each year and will consist of teaching and other duties for the Department of Clinical Medicine. The objective of the position is to complete research training to the level of a doctoral degree. Admission to a PhD programme is a prerequisite for employment, and the programme period starts on commencement of the position. 

The workplace is at UiT in Tromsø. You must be able to start in the position within a reasonable time after receiving the offer.
The project 
Male infertility is an increasing global health concern, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying impaired sperm function remain poorly understood. Previously, our group identified more than 2,000 testis-enriched non-coding RNAs and characterised their expression across germ-cell development. In this project, you will investigate which of these non-coding RNAs persist into mature sperm and whether their expression is associated with sperm quality and fertility. In collaboration with the fertility clinic atthe University Hospital of North Norway (UNN), you will analyse sperm samples from fertility patients and healthy donors. Using sperm phenotyping, cell sorting and RNA sequencing, you will examine differences in non-coding RNA expression between sperm populations with different functional characteristics, including motility and morphology. Selected transcripts will also be investigated in matched testicular tissue using imaging and in situ hybridisation to study their expression during germcell development. By integrating molecular and clinical data, the project aims to identify non-coding RNA signatures associated with sperm health and their potential as biomarkers of male fertility.

jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 8,6000 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
The PHASE Group at the Department of Chemical Engineering at NTNU has a vacant PhD position in which experimental techniques in microfluidics and lab-scale flotation will be used to investigate the recovery of solid mineral particles via bubble formation. The work is part of the project MINBUBBLE funded by the Det Norske Veritas Foundation. The PhD candidate will collaborate with researchers within the PHASE group and at KTH Royal Institute of Technology who will investigate the system with computational methods.

Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department.
About the project
MINBUBBLE: Mineral-Driven Bubble Nucleation for Critical Raw Materials Recovery in Flotation tackles fundamental scientific questions in how mineral particles can be better recovered. Sustainable access to critical raw materials is an environmental and geopolitical imperative, and current mineral extraction and refining methods are inadequate to meet these demands. Specifically, the recovery of minerals using froth flotation struggles to capture the finest fraction of particles due to insufficient attachment of particles to the bubbles. Worsening quality of ores also means that finer fractions are more commonly encountered in operations. 

To recover the fines, one solution may be to abruptly decrease the pressure of the system and initiate bubble formation directly on the mineral particle surfaces. This process is known as dissolved gas flotation (DGF), but it is not used in industrial mineral recovery due to a persistent lack of knowledge regarding the physicochemical processes that drive DGF. At NTNU, experimental work using microfluidics and a lab-scale flotation setup is planned to provide new data and understanding of the generation of bubbles in the presence of different minerals and varying water properties. Together, the experimental and computational results will establish the viability of DGF for extracting critical raw materials as a new, sustainable approach.

The project MINBUBBLE is led by Associate Professor Nadia Shardt in collaboration with Professor Gisle Øye at NTNU and Assistant Professor Shahab Mirjalili at KTH. It is funded under the call topic “Critical Raw Materials” by the Det Norske Veritas Foundation.
Duties of the position
• Complete the doctoral education until a doctorate is obtained.

• You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works.
• You must have excellent written and oral English language skills.
The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria

Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education.

The employment period is 3 years for the doctoral work with a preferred start date in May 2027, but no later than August 2027.
